name: Kuala Lumpur
description: Kuala Lumpur offers a comfortable introduction to Southeast Asia for senior travelers. English is widely spoken, infrastructure is modern, and the city is very affordable. The KL Hop-On Hop-Off bus and Go KL free city buses make sightseeing easy, while the massive shopping malls provide air-conditioned comfort with great accessibility. The city's multicultural food scene means there's something for every palate.

topSpots.name: Petronas Towers & KLCC Park
topSpots.notes: Elevator to skybridge (accessible), park at base with flat paved paths, water fountains, benches everywhere

topSpots.name: Batu Caves (cable car)
topSpots.notes: New cable car service means no need to climb 272 steps, amazing Hindu temple inside the cave

topSpots.name: Islamic Arts Museum
topSpots.notes: Beautiful museum with accessible galleries, restaurant with great views, wheelchair friendly throughout

topSpots.name: Lake Gardens (Perdana Botanical Gardens)
topSpots.notes: Vast green space with flat paths, lakeside benches, butterfly park and bird park nearby, tram service available

topSpots.name: KL Bird Park
topSpots.notes: World's largest free-flight walk-in aviary, flat paved paths, shaded walkways, benches throughout

transport: Go KL City Bus FREE service covers many tourist areas (purple, green, and red lines). MRT and LRT are modern with elevators at newer stations. Grab is very affordable. KL Hop-On Hop-Off bus is a good option. KL Sentral is a model accessible transit hub. Airport Express train (KLIA Ekspres) is quick and accessible.
healthcare: Excellent: Prince Court Medical Centre, Pantai Hospital, Gleneagles Kuala Lumpur. English-speaking doctors. Affordable medical services. Pharmacies widely available. Dental care is very affordable. International clinics in KLCC and Bangsar areas.
highlights: Modern, accessible transit including free city buses
Very affordable luxury hotels and dining
practicalTips: Use the FREE Go KL buses (purple, green, red lines) for central sightseeing
Stay in the KLCC/Bukit Bintang area for walkable access to main attractions
Visit Petronas Towers early morning for shorter queues (tickets sold from 8:30 AM)
Food courts in shopping malls offer clean, affordable local food with air conditioning
Many attractions offer senior discounts — ask at the ticket counter

name: Da Nang
description: Da Nang is Vietnam's most livable city — a beach destination with a modern airport, wide boulevards, and a beautiful coastline. It's less chaotic than Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, making it ideal for seniors who want beach relaxation with cultural options nearby. My Khe Beach is famous for its gentle waves, and the city's affordable resorts cater well to older travelers.

topSpots.name: My Khe Beach
topSpots.notes: Long flat beachfront promenade, gentle waves, accessible beach access points, cafes and restaurants with seating along the shore

topSpots.name: Marble Mountains (elevator)
topSpots.notes: Elevator to the top means no climbing, cave temples to explore, panoramic views, accessible paths at the summit

topSpots.name: Son Tra Peninsula
topSpots.notes: Scenic drive with viewpoints, Linh Ung Pagoda with giant Lady Buddha statue, flat temple grounds

topSpots.name: Dragon Bridge
topSpots.notes: Iconic bridge, flat walking paths along the river, fire show weekends at 9 PM best viewed from a café

topSpots.name: Linh Ung Pagoda
topSpots.notes: Flat temple grounds, giant Lady Buddha statue viewable from ground level, beautiful gardens, ocean views

transport: Da Nang is walkable along the beach road. Taxis are cheap and metered (Mai Linh and Vinasun are reliable). Grab is available. The airport is small and only 15 minutes from the beach area. Free shuttle buses run along the coast. Da Nang train station connects to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City with accessible services.
healthcare: Good: Da Nang Family Hospital (international standard), Vinmec Da Nang International Hospital, Hoan My Hospital. Adequate for non-emergency care. For complex procedures, consider Bangkok or Singapore. Pharmacies available with limited English. Travel insurance recommended.
highlights: Beautiful, calm beach with gentle waves
Less chaotic than Hanoi or Saigon
Modern international airport with direct flights
Gateway to Hoi An and Hue
practicalTips: Stay in the My Khe Beach area for best walkable access to restaurants and the beach
Visit Marble Mountains early (7:30 AM) before the heat when the elevator opens
The Dragon Bridge breathes fire at 9 PM on Saturday and Sunday evenings
Restaurants along the beach offer set lunch menus at great prices ($5-8)
Da Nang has wide pavements — better for walking than most Vietnamese cities

name: Luang Prabang
description: Luang Prabang is a UNESCO World Heritage town where time seems to stand still. Nestled at the confluence of the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers, this former royal capital is compact, walkable, and deeply peaceful. The early morning alms-giving ceremony is a highlight, and the town's many cafes offer perfect spots for watching the world go by. Limited medical facilities but unmatched tranquility.

topSpots.name: Mount Phousi
topSpots.notes: 200+ steps to the top — recommended only for fit seniors. Skip if mobility limited. Beautiful sunset views from base area

topSpots.name: Kuang Si Waterfalls
topSpots.notes: Lower pools accessible by flat path, turquoise waters, beautiful forest setting, small entry fee

topSpots.name: Royal Palace Museum
topSpots.notes: Flat grounds, beautiful colonial building, fascinating history, accessible entrance, lovely gardens

topSpots.name: Night Market
topSpots.notes: Flat walking area along the main street, handicrafts and textiles, early evening best before crowds

topSpots.name: Mekong River Cruise
topSpots.notes: Gentle boat ride, seated experience, beautiful river views, sunset cruise option with refreshments

transport: Luang Prabang is very walkable in the town center. Tuk-tuks are available for longer trips. The airport is small and 15 minutes from town. Mekong River boats are the traditional transport between towns. Cycling is popular but the town is compact enough for walking at a gentle pace.
healthcare: Limited: Luang Prabang Provincial Hospital — basic care only. International Clinic in town for minor issues. For serious medical needs, evacuation to Vientiane, Bangkok, or Chiang Mai. Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential.
practicalTips: Watch the alms-giving ceremony from a respectful distance (early morning, ~5:30-6 AM)
Take a Mekong sunset cruise — it's a seated experience with beautiful views
Book accommodation in the heritage area for walkable access to everything
Many cafes have riverside seating — perfect for afternoon rest breaks
Bring cash — ATMs are limited and many places don't take cards

name: Siem Reap
description: Siem Reap is the gateway to Angkor Wat, one of the world's most extraordinary temple complexes. While many temples have steep steps, the main temples offer accessible ground-level exploration, and tuk-tuks make getting around easy and fun. The town itself has a buzzing food scene and night market, and the Cambodian people are famously warm and welcoming.

topSpots.name: Angkor Wat (ground level)
topSpots.notes: The iconic temple complex, flat ground-level paths around the moat and outer courtyards, stunning photo opportunities without climbing

topSpots.name: Bayon Temple
topSpots.notes: Famous stone faces, ground-level perimeter paths offer views, some ramps at lower galleries

topSpots.name: Ta Prohm (Tomb Raider temple)
topSpots.notes: Paved central path through the famous tree-root ruins, good accessibility at ground level, morning light is magical

topSpots.name: Angkor National Museum
topSpots.notes: Fully air-conditioned, wheelchair accessible, excellent exhibits, audioguide available, good introduction to Khmer history

topSpots.name: Old Market (Phsar Chas) & Night Market
topSpots.notes: Flat walking area, local crafts and souvenirs, many restaurants with seating, evening entertainment

transport: Tuk-tuks are the main transport — choose covered tuk-tuks for sun protection. Private car with driver is very affordable (~$30-40/day) and recommended for seniors visiting temples. Siem Reap Airport is small and modern. Town is walkable in the central area. Many hotels offer free shuttle to Pub Street.
healthcare: Limited: Royal Angkor International Hospital, several clinics. For serious medical needs, consider Bangkok (1 hr flight) or Singapore. Pharmacies available in town with some English labels. Travel insurance with medical evacuation is strongly recommended.
highlights: Angkor Wat — one of humanity's greatest achievements
Excellent and affordable food scene (Pub Street)
Vibrant night market with local handicrafts
practicalTips: Hire a private car instead of a tuk-tuk for temple tours — air conditioning and cushioning make a big difference
Visit Angkor Wat at sunrise (the reflection in the pond is visible from ground level — no climbing needed)
Buy a multi-day pass (3 days for $62) to explore at a relaxed pace
Many restaurants in Siem Reap offer Khmer cuisine with Western adaptations — ask for mild versions
Book a hotel with a pool — it's essential for afternoon rests
